description_full: Sany Heavy Industry Co.,Ltd engages in the research and development, manufacture, and sale of construction machinery in Chinese mainland and internationally. It operates through six segments: Concrete Machinery, Excavating Machinery, Hoisting Machinery, Piling Machinery, Road Machinery, and Financial Services. The company offers concrete pump trucks, concrete delivery pumps, and wall grabs; truck mounted concrete, trailer, and line pump, as well as placing boom, truck mixer, and batching plant; and excavator, such as mini, small, medium, large, long-reach, and wheel excavators. It also provides truck, all-terrain, rough-terrain, truck-mounted, crawler, tower, and loader cranes; roller, motor grader, paver, milling machine, and asphalt batching plant machineries; and dump truck. In addition, the company offers rotary drilling rig, hydraulic grab, and trench cutter; water tower, foam, aerial platform, and water mist fire trucks; and construction machinery product loans, finance lease, and interbank lending and borrowing among financial institutions. Further, it provides maintenance services; and MySANY, a mobile app for SANY Group customers. Additionally, the company manufactures and sells pile drivers. Sany Heavy Industry Co.,Ltd was founded in 1994 and is headquartered in Beijing, China.

financial_summary: Sany Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. is a large-cap industrials business with a $86.8B market cap on $13.5B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +2.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 27%.

The business throws off $2.6B in free cash flow — roughly 19 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.38× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 20× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital.
